newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Namco expands mining into Angola, Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Namco expands mining into Angola, Zaire.

text.p: Canadian and Namibian-listed Namibian Minerals Corporation (Namco) said on Tuesday it was expanding its diamond operations into Angola and Zaire.
The group said in a statement it had acquired a minimum 42.5 percent stake in three diamond concessions covering 664 square km in Angola's northeastern Lunda Norte province.
The concession agreement was subject to approval and required an investment of $2.5 million.
Namco said it planned to dredge the river deposits and explore the alluvial flats.

"The concessions are well located with one area downstream from the Catoca pipe where production by Endiama/Odebrecht/Almazy Rossii-Sakha is planned to commence next year at the rate of five million carats per annum," Namco said.

The Catoca kimberlite pipe, believed to be one of the world's largest kimberlite deposits, is being mined jointly by Angola's state diamond company Endiama, Brazil's Odebrecht and Russia's Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS).
Namco said in Zaire it has acquired a 70 percent interest in 10 exploration licences and one mining permit covering 262 square km in the Wamba/Tunduala district of the Kwango sub-region.

The project is 500 km from the capital Kinshasa and 25 km from the Angolan border. It said preliminary work had yielded limited results with diamond values of $110 per carat. An initial exploration programme costing up to $600,000 was planned.
"In view of the current political situation in Zaire, the company is monitoring its commitment but regards the acquisition as a strategic holding in a potentially productive area," Namco said.
The group also said its Namibian marine diamond mining project was on track.

On its Namibian operation, Namco said it had chartered a vessel for five years and it was being modified at Bremerhaven in Germany. It would be renamed the Kovambo and was expected to arrive in Cape Town in July.
The company's mining system, an 85 tonne underwater tracked vehicle that can work in water depths of up to 200 meters, should be ready by August.
Namco chief executive Alastair Holberton said that the project's first diamond production was due later this year.
